title: decouple-retry-policy-and-upgrade-redis-client
creator: Asha Patel
description: Refactor async worker retry and backpressure handling by extracting a pluggable RetryPolicy interface, upgrading the Redis client to the maintained 5.x series, and cleaning up allocation hotspots in the worker loop. Goal is to reduce tail-latency spikes during traffic bursts, make retry semantics configurable per queue, and make the behavior easier to test and reason about.
acceptance_criteria: RetryPolicy is a first-class interface with unit tests and two implementations (exponential-backoff-with-jitter, fixed-window-budget) integrated into Redis and Kafka consumers
Redis client upgraded across services with no behavior regressions; compatibility shim added for cluster vs standalone pipeline semantics
Worker shutdown path performs graceful draining with controlled concurrency and emits a 'worker.drain' metric
Backpressure coordinator centralizes token-buckets and exposes per-queue metrics (queue_length, inflight, retry_budget)
End-to-end benchmark shows >=30% reduction in p99 worker-loop allocations and <=10% delta in median latency under 3x baseline load
Integration tests for poison-message handling and retry budget exhaustion are added and stable in CI
implementation_notes: Start with a small spike to extract RetryPolicy from consumer loops and validate with unit tests across both Kafka and Redis adapters
Upgrade redis client in a feature branch; introduce a compatibility layer for pipeline/transaction API changes between 4.x and 5.x
Introduce a backpressure coordinator that manages a shared token-bucket per queue; consumers request tokens before processing messages
Replace frequent ephemeral map and string allocations in the hot path with preallocated buffers and pools; measure allocations with runtime profiler
Add histogram + percentile metrics for queueing and processing latency (labels: queue, model, region) and wire into existing tracing
Rollout behind a feature flag (worker.retry.policy_v2) with automatic fallback to legacy policy on errors
